pr.title: Give `trip enter` a fresh shell after you log out, not the dead session
pr.head: 4cfa84b0d3afc1fd74d3803d379c12af48dfa117

summary: trip runs a daemon that keeps terminal sessions alive while clients attach to and detach from them. When a session's command exits, such as a shell you leave with Ctrl-D, the daemon keeps the session as an exited session (the code calls it a corpse) until the next SIGCHLD sweep removes it, so that trip attach can still show what the command left on screen.

That gap broke trip enter <name>. It attaches first and creates the session only when the attach reports the name missing, so right after a logout it attached to the exited session: you saw the old screen, keystrokes went nowhere, and the client never returned. A remote mosh host -- trip enter <name> hung instead of giving you a new shell.

This change gives the Attach request a live flag. enter sets it, and the daemon then removes an exited session that no client holds before it looks the name up, so enter falls through to creating a fresh session. From inside another session, enter sends SwitchSession instead, and that handler now always removes such a session before deciding whether to spawn one. Every other attach passes live: false and still shows an exited session. trip send to an exited session now fails instead of reporting success.

Review history: the first review found that the in-session path still switched you onto the exited session, and the next head fixed it. This head takes that review's two suggestions. SwitchSession clears the session without a flag, and the in-session test waits for the switch instead of sleeping.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Exited session (corpse): a session whose command has ended but which the daemon still holds in its map, showing the command's final screen.
  • Unheld: no client is attached to the session, so client_count() == 0.
  • SIGCHLD sweep: the daemon's reap_children loop, which marks a session exited and removes exited sessions no client holds. It runs only when some child of the daemon exits.
  • live: the new Attach field. When true, an unheld exited session counts as missing.

cards.title: Compatibility
cards.html:
• live on Attach is #[serde(default)], so an older client's request reads as live: false.
  • SwitchSession clears an unheld exited session with no flag, so an older client's in-session enter gets the fix too.
  • Request does not deny unknown fields, so an older daemon ignores live.
  • The running daemon needs a restart on the new binary for the fix to apply.

groups.title: The live flag on the wire
groups.kicker: A new field on the Attach request says the caller needs a running session.
intro: The client and daemon talk in JSON control frames whose shapes live in src/daemon/protocol.rs. The Attach request gains live, a boolean that defaults to false, so the wire format stays readable by both older and newer binaries. SwitchSession needs no field, because the daemon always clears there.

groups.title: The daemon clears an unheld exited session
groups.kicker: Attach with live, and every SwitchSession, remove the corpse first; send refuses an exited session.
intro: The daemon now has one helper, remove_unheld_corpse, that drops a named session when its command has exited and no client holds it. CreateSession already did this inline, and now calls the helper. The Attach handler calls it when live is set, before the loop that looks the name up, so the lookup reports session '<name>' not found and the client creates the session. The SwitchSession handler, which only enter sends, calls it every time before it decides whether to spawn to, so it spawns a fresh session instead of switching the terminal onto the exited one.
SendInput now answers an exited session with session '<name>' has exited (<code>), because nothing reads that session's input any more.

checks.text: A session held by a client, such as one a trip attach viewer is watching, is never cleared. Only a session that nobody is looking at is replaced.

files.note: Extracts remove_unheld_corpse, calls it from Attach when live is set and from every SwitchSession, and makes SendInput refuse an exited session.

checks.text: SendInput has one sender, trip send, so the new error reaches no other caller. Checked by searching every use of Request::SendInput.

From inside session work, trip enter shell after logging out of shell gives a live shell that runs typed input. Checked with a reproduction in a temporary HOME against this head's binary; the same reproduction showed the old logout screen at the previous head.

groups.title: Callers choose live or not
groups.kicker: Only enter's first attach asks for a live session.
intro: attach::attach takes a new live argument, and every caller passes it explicitly. enter passes true on its first attach, then false on the attach after it creates the session, so a command that exits at once is still shown rather than cleared and reported missing. From inside a session, enter sends SwitchSession unchanged, and the daemon does the clearing. trip attach, trip new, and trip wrap pass false, so deliberate viewing of an exited session is unchanged.

files.note: enter asks for a live session on its first attach and shows whatever it created on the attach after a create.

checks.text: When TRIP_SESSION is set, enter returns earlier through SwitchSession, so this live attach runs only from a terminal that is not already in a session.

files.note: attach takes live and puts it on the request.
trip wrap builds its own Attach request and passes live: false.

groups.title: Documentation and the end-to-end check
groups.kicker: The README describes the new behavior, and a new script reproduces the logout case.
intro: The README now says that trip enter <name> treats an exited session as missing, from a plain terminal or from inside another session, that trip attach shows an exited session's last screen, and that trip send fails on one. tests/exited_session_e2e.py runs its own daemon in a temporary HOME, logs out of a /bin/sh session, enters it again with no trip ls in between, both directly and from inside another session, and checks that the new shell is live.

checks.text: At this head, cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo test (132 passed), tests/switcher_e2e.py, and tests/screen_panic_e2e.py pass, and all eight checks of tests/exited_session_e2e.py passed three runs in a row.

files.note: Documents the new behavior of enter, attach, and send on an exited session.
New end-to-end check for entering a session again after logging out of it, directly and from inside another session.

checks.text: The wait for the bare shell title cannot match early. The trip enter process's own title passes through the work client's title rewriter and reaches the terminal as work shell. Only the switch's SessionName handler writes shell. Checked by capturing a run's output, which shows the two titles in that order.
